title: Myths: status, herding and yield
objectives: Answer five client myths with the bias behind each and the response.
body_md:
“PMS and AIFs always beat mutual funds.” Bias: authority / exclusivity. Respond: “Some do and some don't. Let's compare after-fee returns and risk over a full cycle.” “My friend got 30% in an AIF; I want in.” Bias: herd, recency. Respond: “Let's look at the fund's whole track record, lock-in and fees, and whether it fits your plan.” “Mutual funds are for small investors.” Bias: status bias. Respond: “Many large investors keep their core in mutual funds because they're liquid, low-cost and diversified.” “I'll put everything in private credit for the higher yield.” Bias: overconfidence, ignoring risk. Respond: “Higher yield usually means higher credit and liquidity risk. Let's size it as a slice, not the whole.” “Why can't I withdraw from my AIF?” Bias: forgotten lock-in. Respond: “Cat I and II AIFs are closed-ended; money returns as investments are exited. That's why we only use money you won't need.”

| Client says | The bias behind it | Respond with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "PMS and AIFs always beat mutual funds." | Authority / exclusivity | "Some do and some don't. Let's compare after-fee returns and risk over a full cycle." |
| "My friend got 30% in an AIF; I want in." | Herd, recency | "Let's look at the fund's whole track record, lock-in and fees, and whether it fits your plan." |
| "Mutual funds are for small investors." | Status bias | "Many large investors keep their core in mutual funds because they're liquid, low-cost and diversified." |
| "I'll put everything in private credit for the higher yield." | Overconfidence, ignoring risk | "Higher yield usually means higher credit and liquidity risk. Let's size it as a slice, not the whole." |
| "Why can't I withdraw from my AIF?" | Forgotten lock-in | "Cat I and II AIFs are closed-ended; money returns as investments are exited. That's why we only use money you won't need." |

> **Investor takeaway:** Exclusive doesn't mean better. Choose by fit, cost and liquidity.
example: “My friend got 30% in an AIF”: look at the whole track record, lock-in and fees, and whether it fits the plan — not one friend's return.
say: Some do and some don't. Compare after-fee returns over a full cycle.
Many large investors keep their core in mutual funds.
never: PMS and AIFs always beat mutual funds.
Mutual funds are only for small investors.
